About · Funding and selection

Who pays for Norantz, and how reports are chosen

Funding

[PLACEHOLDER] No funding policy yet (open questions §2, item 4). This section will name every funder, the amount band, and what funders may and may not influence. Proposed default: no funder sees or shapes a review before publication.

Which reports are listed

The catalogue aims to list every national report that sets out a long-horizon future for a country: visions with an end state ten or more years out, and scenario sets. Ordinary medium-term plans are not listed.

[PLACEHOLDER] Wording follows the proposed default for method decision 15 (scope), not yet agreed.

Which listed reports are reviewed first

Reports are chosen for review by how much they still shape policy, how far into their horizon they are, and whether there is enough official data to test them.

[PLACEHOLDER] Selection criteria not agreed. You can suggest a report.

By Plural Futures

Norantz (Basque for “towards where?”) is a second reading of national futures, by Plural Futures. It reads each report on its own terms, describes rather than grades, and shows its sources, coverage, and method on every page.

Reviews on this site are drafted with generative AI and may contain errors. Read them as a conversation starter and a starting point for deeper, human-led analysis.

Read generously. Check rigorously.
